title: Senior Manager, Solutions Architecture
Engineering Manager, Preparedness
description:
About the Team

The Preparedness Engineering team is responsible for building and operating safeguards for frontier model risks, to safely enable advanced capabilities while detecting and limiting harm.

About the Role

We’re looking for an engineering manager to lead a team building software systems that detect and prevent harmful misuse of frontier AI models—before incidents occur. This is a builder’s role: you’ll lead engineers shipping production services, detection pipelines, and mitigation mechanisms that protect frontier model integrity and reduce high-severity misuse risk.

While this work intersects with frontier model development, security and risk, we’re explicitly seeking someone with a software engineering foundation who is comfortable building reliable systems that can operate at billions of users scale.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

 - Lead a team of software engineers building detection + mitigation systems for frontier model harms.

 - Set the technical roadmap and execution strategy: prioritize, design, ship, iterate, measure impact.

 - Build production systems: services, pipelines, tooling, instrumentation, and automation that scale with frontier model usage.

 - Partner deeply with Research and Product to translate evolving model capabilities into concrete tests, signals, and mitigations that can be deployed at scale.

 - Drive strong engineering fundamentals: architecture, reliability, monitoring, performance, and operational excellence.

 - Hire and grow an exceptional team across backend, data systems, and applied ML engineering domains as needed.

 - Anticipate what breaks at scale as agentic workflows become more capable.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Experience building systems in adversarial, fast-evolving environments

 - Thrive in high context environments

 - Are comfortable with ambiguity and novelty

 - Communicate clearly and build trust quickly with senior stakeholders—pragmatic, collaborative, and calm under scrutiny.

 - Significant experience leading engineering teams and delivering production systems end-to-end.

 - Strong technical judgment in system design, distributed systems, data pipelines, observability, and operational reliability.

 - Demonstrated ability to partner cross-functionally with Research/Product/Security to ship systems that materially reduce risk or abuse at scale.

 - Background in autonomy, high-scale real-time systems, or intelligence-adjacent technical domains is a plus.

Compensation Programs & Operations Lead
description:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Compensation team helps attract, reward, and retain the people advancing our mission to ensure that artificial general intelligence benefits all of humanity. We develop compensation strategies and programs that support a rapidly evolving business, combining market insight, sound judgment, and thoughtful execution. We partner across People, Finance, Legal, and the business to deliver programs that employees and leaders can understand and trust.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Compensation Programs & Operations Lead to own the end-to-end program management of our cyclical and ad hoc compensation programs globally. You will turn compensation priorities into executable plans and lead delivery from initial scoping through launch, reconciliation, and continuous improvement.

This is a senior, hands-on role for a compensation subject-matter expert who is energized by operations and E2E program ownership. You should bring experience across compensation operations analysis, compensation analysis, business partnership, and program management. Having done this work yourself, you understand the practical details behind compensation decisions and what it takes to implement them accurately.

You will establish how our compensation programs run: the calendar, responsibilities, systems requirements, controls, communications, and handoffs that connect program design to the employee experience. You’ll partner closely with Compensation Partners, HR Business Partners, People Operations, People Technology, Finance, Payroll, Equity Administration, and Legal, creating clarity and driving execution as priorities evolve.

In this role, you will:

 - Lead our compensation program portfolio. Own the integrated roadmap and calendar for cyclical and ad hoc programs, including compensation reviews, bonus and equity cycles, promotion-related compensation processes, recognition and retention initiatives, and new program launches.

 - Drive programs from planning through completion. Define scope, deliverables, milestones, accountable owners, dependencies, and resource needs. Coordinate work across teams, resolve blockers, and bring decisions and tradeoffs to the right owners early.

 - Translate compensation expertise into practical operations. Work with Compensation Partners and program owners to turn approved designs into clear eligibility rules, calculations, workflows, approval paths, and exception processes. Identify gaps and implementation risks before launch.

 - Stay close to the analysis and data. Build and review models, validate inputs and calculations, investigate discrepancies, and reconcile final outcomes. Be comfortable working directly in the details when a program needs it.

 - Build reliable execution controls. Establish quality checks, documented approvals, access controls, and audit trails. Coordinate accurate handoffs to Payroll, Equity Administration, and People Operations, with clear ownership through completion.

 - Shape compensation systems and tooling. Translate business needs into requirements, partner with People Technology on configuration and integrations, lead user acceptance testing, and prioritize improvements that reduce manual work and errors.

 - Manage incoming requests and changing priorities. Create a practical intake and prioritization process for ad hoc compensation initiatives. Make capacity, timing, and dependencies visible so urgent work can be delivered alongside recurring commitments.

 - Make programs easier to understand and use. Develop operating guides, manager resources, communications, and training. Equip Compensation Partners and other stakeholders to explain programs consistently and resolve questions efficiently.

 - Improve how the function operates. Measure accuracy, timeliness, manual effort, and stakeholder experience. Run post-cycle reviews and turn findings into simpler processes, stronger documentation, and effective automation.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have 10+ years of progressive compensation experience, including substantial responsibility for global compensation programs and operations in a complex, fast-growing organization.

 - Have performed the core responsibilities of a Compensation Operations Analyst, Compensation Analyst, Compensation Partner, and Compensation Program Manager, whether through separate roles or a combination of positions.

 - Bring deep compensation expertise across base pay, incentives, equity, market benchmarking, salary structures, and job architecture, and understand how these elements translate into day-to-day administration.

 - Have independently led complex compensation cycles and new initiatives, coordinating multiple teams from planning and analysis through implementation and reconciliation.

 - Are deliberately drawn to an operations-focused role. You enjoy making programs work, improving the details, and building processes that others can rely on.

 - Combine strong analytical skills with practical systems experience, including advanced spreadsheet modeling and hands-on work with Workday or comparable HR and compensation platforms.

 - Can establish priorities and drive progress when requirements are incomplete or changing, while making thoughtful tradeoffs about speed, accuracy, and capacity.

 - Communicate clearly with senior leaders and working teams, influence across functions, and make ownership and next steps explicit.

 - Exercise sound judgment with confidential information and bring a high standard of accuracy, accountability, and service to your work.

title: Head of First Party Chip Finance
description:
About the Role

As Head of First Party Chip Finance, you will be the finance leader for OpenAI’s custom silicon efforts. You will partner with teams across chip design, engineering, infrastructure, supply chain, and finance to turn technical roadmaps into sound investment decisions and financially disciplined execution.

This role spans the full chip development lifecycle: evaluating design and roadmap choices, building investment cases, forecasting development and production costs, and supporting manufacturing and deployment at scale. You will give leadership a clear view of program economics, funding requirements, and risks as we build first-party compute capabilities.

In this role, you will:

 - Lead financial evaluation of custom silicon programs, including development investment, production economics, deployment assumptions, and expected returns. Assess first-party chips against alternative compute options.

 - Build and own program-level models and multiyear forecasts that connect engineering milestones, development spending, manufacturing volumes, supplier commitments, and cash requirements.

 - Partner closely with chip-design and engineering leaders on technical decisions that affect performance, power consumption, cost, and time to deployment. Translate complex design tradeoffs into clear financial recommendations.

 - Develop a detailed view of chip and system costs, including wafers, manufacturing yields, packaging, memory, testing, and integration. Identify opportunities to improve economics as programs move from development into production.

 - Partner with Supply Chain and Procurement on supplier strategy and commercial negotiations, including capacity reservations, volume commitments, prepayments, and contractual risk.

 - Work with Treasury, Corporate Finance, Accounting, Tax, and Legal to evaluate financing and payment structures, manage financial exposure, and support program execution.

 - Support commercial deployment and pricing decisions through analysis of unit economics, total cost of ownership, and the relationship between technical performance and economic value.

 - Establish budgets, reporting, and financial controls that give engineering and finance leaders timely visibility into spending, commitments, milestones, and emerging risks. Build a small, high-performing team while remaining directly involved in the analysis.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

 - Prior experience leading finance for semiconductor or custom silicon programs. You have directly owned investment analysis, program budgets, and financial decisions across chip development and production.

 - An undergraduate degree in a technical discipline, preferably electrical engineering or computer science. An MBA or equivalent business experience complements your technical foundation.

 - 10+ years of experience across semiconductor finance, hardware finance, strategic finance, or related fields, with substantial responsibility for complex technical programs.

 - Strong command of semiconductor economics, including development costs, manufacturing yields, packaging and memory costs, production ramps, and supplier commitments.

 - Excellent financial modeling skills and the ability to independently build models, test technical and commercial assumptions, quantify uncertainty, and recommend a path forward.

 - The technical credibility to work closely with chip designers and engineering leaders, understand their constraints, and evaluate tradeoffs across performance, power, cost, and timing.

 - Experience supporting supplier negotiations, prepayments, and major investment commitments in partnership with supply chain and finance teams.

 - A hands-on operating style, clear communication, and the judgment to introduce financial discipline while helping technical teams move quickly. You use technology and AI to improve analysis and decision-making.

 - A strong track record of hiring, leading, and developing high-performing teams.

title: B2B Ecosystem Lead, Partner Growth
description:
About the Team

We are a small and fast-moving B2B partnerships team that shapes and executes OpenAI’s most important collaborations. We work across the B2B ecosystem, including software vendors, technology platforms, and services partners, to help them bring useful AI offerings to market and reach more business customers. Working closely with Sales, Product, and partner programs, we build channels and repeatable go-to-market approaches that expand customer choice and adoption of OpenAI’s models and products.

About the Role

As a B2B Ecosystem Partnerships Lead focused on Partner Growth, you will own the onboarding, activation, and growth of a partner portfolio across OpenAI’s expanding ecosystem programs, including marketplace and Sign in with ChatGPT. This is a hands-on individual contributor role centered on partner management, joint go-to-market execution, and commercial growth. Your portfolio may span ISVs, technology platforms,, and other B2B partners as opportunities evolve. You bring a generalist’s range across relationships, business analysis, deal execution, and operational problem solving. You will build repeatable ways to support a growing partner base and take on selected strategic partnerships.

In this role, you will:

 - Identify and recruit partners across B2B segments for ecosystem programs and joint go-to-market opportunities, prioritizing customer needs, product fit, commercial potential, and readiness to participate and grow.

 - Own day-to-day relationships across your partner portfolio, tailoring engagement to partner needs and opportunity while using repeatable approaches to support a growing partner base.

 - Develop practical business and account plans with partners and Sales, with clear use cases, target customers, owners, milestones, and adoption and commercial goals.

 - Negotiate product and commercial agreements with Legal, Finance, and Product, and lead selected high-touch strategic opportunities in coordination with other partnership owners.

 - Guide partners through program onboarding, technical evaluation, integration, and activation; coordinate enablement and resolve barriers to launch, sustained usage, and expansion.

 - Execute co-selling, joint marketing, and marketplace opportunities with account teams; coordinate with cloud and other ecosystem partners where they help customers buy and deploy solutions.

 - Run regular partner reviews, identify inactive or stalled partners, and execute growth plans that improve participation, product adoption, customer demand, and relationship health.

 - Track onboarding completion, time to activation, active partners, product usage, pipeline contribution, and commercial results with Sales and Operations; use the data to focus effort.

 - Improve onboarding materials, enablement, and partner engagement practices with program and product teams; turn recurring partner issues into fixes that help the broader ecosystem scale.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

 - 8+ years of experience in partnerships, business development, partner or account management, enterprise sales, or related commercial roles in technology.

 - Experience managing and growing a portfolio of B2B partners or accounts, with measurable results in onboarding, adoption, retention, or commercial expansion.

 - An understanding of B2B business models, partner channels, and how companies bring products and services to market. Experience with ISVs, technology platforms, services partners, or cloud marketplaces is a plus.

 - Strong business judgment and analytical skills: you can assess partner economics, prioritize a portfolio, and build repeatable processes that help more partners succeed.

 - Ability to work across Product, Engineering, Sales, Marketing, Legal, and Finance, build trust with partner teams, and drive progress without formal authority.

 - A generalist mindset, curiosity about AI, and the ability to learn new products and markets quickly. You can discuss integrations with technical teams and connect capabilities to customer value.

 - Clear communication, sound negotiation skills, and reliable follow-through. You are comfortable balancing relationship building, structured planning, and hands-on problem solving in a changing environment.

title: Senior Principal Forward Deployed Engineer, Frontier Engineering
description:
At Snowflake, we are powering the era of the agentic enterprise. To usher in this new era, we seek AI-native thinkers across every function who are energized by the opportunity to reinvent how they work. You don’t just use tools; you possess an innate curiosity, treating AI as a high-trust collaborator that is core to how you solve problems and accelerate your impact. We look for low-ego individuals who thrive in dynamic and fast-moving environments and move with an experimental mindset — who rapidly test emerging capabilities to discover simpler, more powerful ways to deliver results. At Snowflake, your role isn't just to execute a function, but to help redefine the future of how work gets done.

Snowflake is about empowering enterprises to achieve their full potential, and people too. With a culture that's all in on impact, innovation, and collaboration, Snowflake is the sweet spot for building big, moving fast, and taking technology and careers to the next level.

We are hiring a Principal Forward Deployed Engineer II for our Frontier Engineering team. This team embeds directly with Snowflake's most strategic customers to design, build, and deploy production-grade AI systems . At the IC6 level, you serve as the senior technical authority and architectural leader for a portfolio of high-impact customer engagements. You operate as a peer technical advisor to CTOs, VPs of Engineering, chief architects, and heads of data and AI, setting technical direction that extends beyond individual accounts and influences how Snowflake delivers AI solutions at scale.




AS A PRINCIPAL FORWARD DEPLOYED ENGINEER II YOU WILL:

 - Serve as the senior technical authority and architectural leader for customer engineering leadership: Build durable, peer-level relationships with CTOs, VPs of Engineering, chief architects, and heads of data and AI at Snowflake’s most strategic accounts. Lead architectural steering, technical reviews, and executive strategy alignment while shaping multi-year AI roadmaps across a portfolio of customers.

 - Drive Architecture and Technical Strategy Across a Portfolio of High-Stakes Deployments: Set the technical strategy, architecture, and execution model across multiple complex, high-visibility AI engagements. Own end-to-end outcomes, arbitrate the most difficult cross-system tradeoffs, and establish patterns that scale across customers, teams, and business units.

 - Influence Snowflake Product Direction: Translate recurring customer needs and deployment learnings into clear product requirements, partner with Product and Engineering leaders, and drive adoption of capabilities that improve outcomes across the field.

 - Stay hands-on and set the engineering bar: Write production code and working prototypes on the most critical or ambiguous parts of customer programs, review designs and code, and demonstrate the technical depth and judgment expected across the organization.

 - Set the AI quality and reliability bar: Define organization-level standards for evaluation, observability, reliability, security, guardrails, and responsible deployment. Turn ambiguous customer goals into clear, testable measures and ensure those standards are applied consistently across engagements.

 - Provide technical leadership and develop senior technical talent: Mentor Principal, Staff, and Senior engineers; develop technical leads; raise engineering standards across the organization; and lead through influence across Engineering, Product, Sales, and other cross-functional teams.

 - Travel to Customer Sites: Spend at least 25% of your time onsite working with customers.


OUR IDEAL CANDIDATE WILL HAVE:

 - 15+ years of software engineering experience, including a sustained track record of building and shipping production AI/ML or agentic systems at enterprise scale.

 - Proven track record serving as a trusted technical advisor to CTOs and executive engineering leaders at large enterprises, and setting technical direction across multiple strategic accounts or enterprise programs.

 - Demonstrated success converting client and field delivery patterns into reusable platforms, tools, frameworks, reference architectures, or open-source libraries adopted across teams or customers.

 - Deep expertise in production AI architectures—including RAG pipelines, multi-step agentic systems, evaluation frameworks, guardrails, observability, security, and operating models for enterprise-scale adoption.

 - Hands-on technical leader who writes and reviews production code, stays close to implementation, and can move from executive strategy to the critical technical details that determine whether a system succeeds.

 - Exceptional systems thinking and technical communication skills across deeply technical and executive audiences, with the ability to influence without formal authority and align multiple organizations around a common technical strategy.


BONUS POINTS FOR THE FOLLOWING:

 - Experience leading cross-organizational technical initiatives that improve how enterprise AI solutions are designed, deployed, and adopted.

 - Active contributions to open-source AI frameworks, technical publications, or industry speaking engagements.

 - Familiarity with Cortex AI, Snowpark, or modern enterprise data infrastructure platforms.


WHY JOIN FRONTIER ENGINEERING AT SNOWFLAKE?

Frontier Engineering is where Snowflake’s AI platform meets reality. You’re not building demos, you’re shipping AI applications that run in some of the world’s most complex enterprise environments. At the IC6 level, you also define the reusable architectures, engineering standards, and product feedback loops that allow these solutions to scale across customers. You will work on hard problems with real stakes, alongside engineers who are deeply technical and customer-obsessed.

How do you want to make your impact?

Snowflake is growing fast, and we’re scaling our team to help enable and accelerate our growth. We are looking for people who share our values, challenge ordinary thinking, and push the pace of innovation while building a future for themselves and Snowflake.

How do you want to make your impact?

title: Product Marketing, Messaging Lead
description:
About the Team

OpenAI’s B2B Marketing team helps businesses understand, adopt, and get value from our products. We work closely with Product, Research, Sales, and Communications to connect advances in AI to the problems organizations are trying to solve.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Messaging Lead to shape how businesses understand OpenAI and the value of our portfolio. You’ll develop a clear enterprise narrative, connect individual product stories to it, and help explain how AI is changing the way people and organizations work.

You’ll work directly with senior leaders and technical teams to make difficult positioning decisions and turn them into work that customers, executives, and the field can use. You’ll be a hands-on writer and editor as well as a strategic partner, responsible for the quality and coherence of our most important business stories.

This is a senior individual contributor role, with the potential to build and lead a team as the function grows.

In this role, you will:

 - Define and evolve the enterprise narrative and the messages that connect our products to customer needs and business outcomes.

 - Partner with product and industry marketers to make the portfolio clear and differentiated while preserving the depth each audience needs.

 - Translate complex capabilities into precise, compelling stories with Product and Research.

 - Personally develop core enterprise pitches, executive narratives, major launch messages, and other high-priority materials.

 - Bring customer insight, competitive context, and credible proof into the story with GTM and Customer Marketing.

 - Help Marketing, Communications, and Enablement apply the narrative, and improve it through customer feedback and testing.

 - Coach partners on messaging and writing, and help define how the function should grow.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

 - 14+ years of experience in B2B product marketing, positioning, or messaging, with a track record of shaping enterprise narratives and translating complex technology portfolios into clear, differentiated stories for business audiences.

 - A track record of leading messaging, positioning, or product marketing for complex technology portfolios serving business customers.

 - Exceptional writing and editing skills, with examples of work you personally created and an ability to explain the decisions behind it.

 - Strong product and technical judgment, including the ability to distinguish a supported claim from an appealing assertion.

 - Experience working with senior executives and technical leaders, resolving conflicting views, and leading without formal authority.

 - Evidence that your narratives were adopted by customer-facing teams and improved customer understanding or evaluation.

 - The willingness to work hands-on, move through ambiguity, and revise your view when evidence changes.

 - Practical fluency with AI tools and thoughtful judgment about where human review matters.

 - Experience developing marketers or building a messaging function is valuable. Previous people-management experience is not required for the initial IC role.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees. Occasional travel will be required.

title: Staff Software Engineer — Engineering Systems, Continuous Integration
description:
At Snowflake, we are powering the era of the agentic enterprise. To usher in this new era, we seek AI-native thinkers across every function who are energized by the opportunity to reinvent how they work. You don’t just use tools; you possess an innate curiosity, treating AI as a high-trust collaborator that is core to how you solve problems and accelerate your impact. We look for low-ego individuals who thrive in dynamic and fast-moving environments and move with an experimental mindset — who rapidly test emerging capabilities to discover simpler, more powerful ways to deliver results. At Snowflake, your role isn't just to execute a function, but to help redefine the future of how work gets done.


ABOUT SNOWFLAKE

Snowflake is building the AI Data Cloud, enabling organizations around the world to mobilize data and develop applications at global scale. The Engineering Systems organization builds the infrastructure, tools, and platforms that help Snowflake engineers develop, test, and deliver high-quality software efficiently.

The Continuous Integration team is responsible for the systems that power builds, tests, validation, and developer workflows across Snowflake’s engineering organization. As a Staff Software Engineer on this team, you will help define the technical direction of critical CI infrastructure used by thousands of engineers across a rapidly growing, multi-cloud codebase.


AS A STAFF SOFTWARE ENGINEER, YOU WILL

 - Own the technical direction and architecture of large-scale Continuous Integration services and infrastructure.

 - Design, build, and operate distributed systems that support reliable, performant, and secure software delivery.

 - Lead the development of CI capabilities that improve build reliability, test execution, developer productivity, and release velocity.

 - Partner with engineering leadership, product managers, and teams across Snowflake to define quarterly and long-term technical roadmaps.

 - Drive architectural decisions across build systems, test orchestration, resource scheduling, workflow execution, and developer tooling.

 - Identify systemic bottlenecks in the software delivery lifecycle and develop solutions that improve engineering efficiency at scale.

 - Establish high standards for design, code quality, testing, observability, reliability, and operational readiness.

 - Mentor engineers through design reviews, code reviews, technical guidance, and collaborative problem-solving.

 - Lead complex projects involving multiple teams and cross-functional dependencies.

 - Participate in incident response, root-cause analysis, and long-term reliability improvements.

 - Evaluate emerging technologies and industry practices to keep Snowflake’s developer platform scalable and effective.


OUR IDEAL STAFF SOFTWARE ENGINEER WILL HAVE

 - 7+ years of industry experience designing and building production software systems.

 - A track record of technical leadership across complex, multi-team engineering initiatives.

 - Deep experience designing and operating distributed systems at scale.

 - Experience building or significantly evolving enterprise-grade Continuous Integration or Continuous Delivery systems.

 - Strong computer science fundamentals, including data structures, algorithms, distributed systems, and systems design.

 - Proficiency in one or more programming languages such as Java, C++, Python, or Go.

 - Experience making architectural decisions involving scalability, reliability, performance, security, and maintainability.

 - A strong understanding of developer productivity and the software development lifecycle.

 - Excellent problem-solving skills and sound technical judgment.

 - Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain complex technical concepts clearly.

 - A collaborative mindset and a demonstrated ability to mentor and influence engineers across teams.


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Experience with CI/CD and build systems such as Jenkins, GitHub Actions, Bazel, ArgoCD, or comparable platforms.

 - Experience with build optimization, caching, parallel execution, incremental builds, or distributed test scheduling.

 - Experience designing multi-tenant systems with strong isolation, reliability, performance, and security requirements.

 - Experience with Kubernetes, containers, or public cloud platforms such as AWS, Azure, or GCP.

 - Experience operating large-scale developer platforms or engineering infrastructure.

 - Experience with observability, monitoring, alerting, and production operations.

 - Experience authoring technical roadmaps, architecture documents, project plans, postmortems, and root-cause analyses.

 - Experience working with data systems, distributed storage, or cloud-based services.

 - A history of improving engineering practices and multiplying the effectiveness of teams.


WHY ENGINEERING SYSTEMS AT SNOWFLAKE?

 - Build infrastructure that thousands of Snowflake engineers rely on every day.

 - Solve challenging distributed systems and developer productivity problems at significant scale.

 - Help improve the speed, reliability, and quality of software delivery across Snowflake.

 - Work with experienced engineers across a multi-cloud data platform.

 - Influence the technical direction of critical engineering infrastructure.

 - Grow your impact through architecture, mentorship, and cross-team technical leadership.


COMPENSATION

Snowflake is committed to pay equity and transparency. Actual compensation will be determined based on factors including relevant experience, skills, location, and internal equity.

For the US-Market 1 location band, the compensation range for this role is:

 - Base salary: $236,000–$354,000 USD

 - Target bonus: 15%

 - Total target compensation: $271,400–$407,100 USD

 - Equity: Eligible for an RSU grant in addition to base salary and bonus

Snowflake also offers a comprehensive benefits package, including medical, dental, vision, 401(k), ESPP, paid time off, parental leave, disability coverage, and company-paid life insurance.

Every Snowflake employee is expected to follow the company’s confidentiality and security standards for handling sensitive data. Snowflake employees must abide by the company’s data security plan as an essential part of their duties. It is every employee’s responsibility to keep customer information secure and confidential.

Snowflake is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

Snowflake is growing fast, and we’re scaling our team to help enable and accelerate our growth. We are looking for people who share our values, challenge ordinary thinking, and push the pace of innovation while building a future for themselves and Snowflake.

title: Senior Manager, Account Manager, Enterprise
description:
ABOUT RAMP

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $200B in annualized spend flows in and out of 70,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.




ABOUT THE ROLE 

In this role, you will be a front-line manager to a group of Account Managers who are responsible for hunting, pitching, and expanding the existing customer base at Ramp.

You'll lead a group of 6-8 Account Managers, each carrying a book of 60-70 Enterprise customers with real latitude over how they grow it. This is a build role, not a maintain role: the playbooks, coaching systems, and performance bar you set are the ones this team runs on next year. Your ceiling is set by how well you turn individual AM judgment into a repeatable, scalable motion that grows the segment.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Build and run a high-performing team of 6-8 Account Managers - setting the bar for culture, morale, and daily execution.

 - Get embedded in the relationships that matter. Engage directly with key customers and top accounts alongside your team, building trust and long-term partnership.

 - Own the number. Manage quota performance and pipeline generation across your team to hit spend activation, product activation, retention, and expansion goals.

 - Forecast and report team performance to senior leadership with clear-eyed visibility into what's working and what isn't.

 - Hire and develop the next generation of AMs - training on product, buyer personas, competition, and tooling through role-plays, game film, and real deal work.

 - Coach relentlessly. Run daily 1:1s, dissect call feedback, lead enablement sessions, and build career paths for every rep on your team.

 - Turn what works into a system. Continuously refine team processes and tooling to improve output and efficiency as the segment scales.

 - Represent Account Management cross-functionally, partnering with Sales, CX, CSM, Risk, and Product to remove blockers and drive outcomes.




WHAT YOU NEED

 - Minimum 5 years of quota-carrying sales or account management experience as an individual contributor, with a proven, consistent track record of exceeding goals (new business or cross-sell/upsell experience mandatory)

 - Minimum 5 years building and leading account management or sales teams, with a track record of exceeding goal (new business or cross-sell/upsell experience mandatory)

 - Prior success in fast-paced, results-oriented GTM environments, ideally at SaaS or AI companies

 - A genuine passion for hiring, with a thoughtful approach to talent development

 - Ability to articulate contractual, technical, and financial value to customers, including C-Suite and executive leaders

 - Strong track record negotiating, structuring, and executing complex agreements

 - Proficiency with data analytics tools (Salesforce, Looker, Excel) and a bias toward using data to drive decisions

 - Strong collaboration and influencing skills, backed by excellent communication and presentation ability. 

 - High agency and adaptability - no two days are the same, and the only constant is change

 - A desire and willingness to jump headfirst into complex, challenging problems for the good of the business.



Great to Haves

 - Experience at a high-growth, top SaaS/AI startup

title: VP of Sales - Public Sector
description:
WHO ARE WE?

Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company.  We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems.

We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.

We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft.

We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us!

Role Overview

As our VP of Sales - Public Sector, you will spearhead year-over-year revenue growth by developing and executing on enterprise level PUBSEC customer acquisition strategies across the region. You will drive long-term success through strategic development, coaching, and expanding Cohere’s presence in the public sector. In this pivotal leadership role, you will cultivate and guide our sales team to exceed revenue targets and organizational goals, while fostering a culture of excellence and innovation.

Candidates must be based in North America to be considered for this career opportunity.

Key Responsibilities

As our VP of Public Sector Sales you will:

 - Develop, execute, and lead a comprehensive go-to-market growth strategy and sales plan for the Public Sector, driving revenue growth and market expansion working with other regional sales teams.

 - Provide sales and operational leadership to Cohere’s  PUBSEC sales team, ensuring alignment with company objectives and priorities.

 - Partner with Marketing, Product, and Engineering teams to synchronize sales efforts with broader company goals.

 - Represent Cohere at PUBSEC industry events, conferences, and networking opportunities, as well as with regulators and government agencies, in collaboration with other regional and global leaders in Cohere.

 - Manage and nurture relationships with government decision-makers and partners to ensure Cohere’s success in the region. Identify and pursue new business opportunities, negotiating and closing high-value deals.

 - Collaborate with global teams to strengthen anchor relationships and establish best practices for enterprise-level project implementations, ensuring strong client engagement throughout project lifecycles.

Qualifications

This career opportunity may be a good match for you if you:

 - Have 10+ years of PUBSEC sales and leadership experience leading go-to-market efforts and driving revenue growth for fast paced technology organizations.

 - Have an established network, including federal agencies, prime contractors, and industry associations.

 - Possess a proven track record of leading capture and sales efforts for consultative solution sales and business development efforts, with a deep understanding of regional procurement and budget cycles, customer success, and resource allocation.

 - Have exceptional communication and leadership skills, with the ability to build cross-functional relationships and influence at all levels.

 - Are comfortable operating in a matrix environment, coordinating efforts across cross-functional teams and regions without the need for a large direct organization.

 - Are a self-starter with an entrepreneurial mindset, capable of working independently, rolling up sleeves, and driving impact as a ‘builder.’

 - Experience in AI or a related industry is highly desirable.

 - Must be based in North America with willingness to travel (25-40%).


WORKING LOCATION:

This role can be based remotely or from one of our office locations listed on the job description - there is no minimum in-office qualification requirement. We care most about hiring exceptional people regardless of locations, though please check the location listed on the posting for guidance around the core time zone or working hours alignment expected for the role.

 - RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme.

   Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching.

 - 6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days!)

 - Budget for traveling to other offices if you are remote, plus an annual company offsite.




HOW AND WHERE WE WORK:

 - Cohere is remote-friendly, but we also have offices in Toronto, London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul with more opening soon.

 - For those in the office: a daily lunch program, plenty of snacks, and regular community and social events.

 - For those not near an office: a co-working benefit so you can work alongside others in your city.

About the Role

At OpenAI, we are proud to build and operate our data centers with a community-first led approach. From construction to operations, we want to be positive partners within our data center communities that we are honored to call home…and we are just getting started.

OpenAI is seeking a Workforce Development & Education Manager to help build local talent for data center construction, commissioning, and operations in communities hosting OpenAI infrastructure projects. You will work with infrastructure teams and project partners, education providers, and local Community Engagement Leads to understand workforce needs and help education and training providers prepare people for these jobs of the future.

You will build partnerships with local community colleges, technical schools, universities, and union apprenticeship programs from the ground up. Working with educators and technical experts, you will develop and expand training programs that connect local residents with career opportunities and meet the local industry hiring needs.

Key Responsibilities

 - Work in partnership with the local Community Engagement Lead to build and manage relationships with community colleges, technical schools, universities, career and technical education programs, and local workforce boards.

 - Work with building trades unions and joint apprenticeship and training committees to expand training opportunities aligned with project needs both on a local and national level.

 - Partner with OpenAI’s infrastructure teams, developers, contractors, and operators to identify job requirements, skills gaps, and hiring timelines across construction, commissioning, and operations.

 - Work with educators and technical experts to develop or adapt curricula, hands-on training, and credential programs that reflect employer requirements and offerings available through OpenAI’s literacy programs.

 - Support apprenticeships, internships, and other work-based learning opportunities with participating employers.

 - Manage program implementation, including timelines, partner responsibilities, and progress against agreed goals.

 - Track participation, completion, credential attainment, job placement, and retention, working with partners to use the results to improve programs.

title: Head of Mid Market Sales, North America
description:
WHY HARVEY

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.

This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We’re scaling fast and defining a new category in real time. The work is ambitious, the bar is high, and the opportunity for growth — personal, professional, and financial — is unmatched.

Our team moves fast, takes ownership, and is deeply committed to the mission — operating with intensity, staying close to our customers, and pushing each other for excellence. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.




ROLE OVERVIEW

This is a second line leadership role where you will lead frontline managers, build a world class team, and own the regional Mid Market number for North America. You will be responsible for turning strong early traction into a repeatable, high performing got to market engine across legal and professional services.

We are still early. That means you will operate across altitudes, setting strategy, building structure, and staying close to the field on critical deals. You will help define how Harvey shows up in the North American market, shape our sales motion, and ensure we are delivering real value to customers adopting AI in high stakes competitive environments.

We are looking for someone who has led multi team segments, hired and developed high potential sales managers, scaled teams in ambiguity, implemented a rigorous sales playbook, and knows what great looks like in complex SaaS sales.



About the NAMER Mid-Market Segment

Mid Market at Harvey runs an “enter-lite” motion selling to law firms with 15–150 attorneys, including many of the most prestigious speciality and boutique firms in the world. . Reps own the full cycle, prospecting into net-new accounts, converting them, and driving expansion

You'll inherit a team of Mid Market Sales Managers and their AEs based across western NAMER and will be the primary owner of how that motion runs and scales across the region.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Hire, lead, coach and develop a team of Mid Market Sales Managers across North America driving accountability for net new logo and expansion ARR targets.

 - Own and evolve the NAMER Mid-Market playbook end to end- ICP and segmentation criteria, qualification methodology (e.g., MEDDIC/MEDDPICC), deal stage definitions, discounting and deal desk guardrails, and forecasting cadence, so the motion is repeatable across every manager and AE in the region.

 - Implement and maintain a rigorous sales operating cadence, including seller onboarding, enablement, coaching, pipeline generation, and deal execution.

 - Drive the regional sales strategy, including territory design, coverage models, and go-to-market execution across the U.S. and Canada.

 - Own NAMER mid market forecasting and pipeline health, providing accurate reporting to senior leadership.

 - Hire, coach, and retain top managerial talent; build a strong leadership bench across the region.

 - Partner with global mid market leadership (EMEA and APAC) to keep the playbook, methodology, and comp/accelerator structure consistent globally while localizing it for NAMER buyer behavior and legal market dynamics.

 - Develop executive relationships with Harvey's highest value Mid Market customers across the region.

 - Work cross functionally with marketing, solutions engineering, legal, and customer success to ensure a cohesive customer experience across the region.

 - Represent NAMER mid market in global planning cycles, headcount discussions, and strategic initiatives.




WHAT YOU HAVE

 - 10+ years of B2B tech sales experience, including 4+ years hiring, managing and developing sales managers or senior individual contributors.

 - Demonstrated success leading a regional or multi market sales organization in a high-growth, early stage environment.

 - Strong track record of selling complex software to enterprise or mid market clients using a consultative, value based methodology.

 - Experience building or scaling a sales playbook : segmentation, qualification frameworks (MEDDIC/MEDDPICC or equivalent), territory design, and deal-desk processes, in a fast growing SaaS environment.

 - Genuine passion for Harvey's mission and a strong interest in how AI is transforming knowledge work and the legal profession.

title: Marketplace Lead
description:
About the Role
We are a small, fast-moving partnerships team that shapes and executes OpenAI’s most important collaborations. Your mission is to build the product, operating systems, and capabilities that will power OpenAI’s B2B marketplace. You will define the marketplace product strategy and translate it into a clear roadmap, scalable tooling, and an operating model through which customers can discover, evaluate, purchase, deploy, and manage trusted third-party solutions built on and with OpenAI’s models.

You are a senior marketplace builder with strong product judgment, operational rigor, and a track record of developing B2B platforms at scale. You are comfortable moving between product strategy, marketplace operations, commercial models, data, and systems design. You can turn ambiguous customer and partner needs into clear priorities and build the infrastructure required to support a trusted, high-quality marketplace.

Key Responsibilities:

 - Define the vision, strategy, roadmap, and success metrics for OpenAI’s B2B marketplace.

 - Translate customer, partner, and business needs into clear product requirements and priorities in close partnership with product and engineering.

 - Design the end-to-end marketplace experience and operating architecture, including partner onboarding, catalog management, discovery, evaluation, procurement, private offers, billing, deployment, identity, governance, and lifecycle management.

 - Build the internal and external tools required to operate the marketplace efficiently, including workflows for solution intake, review, approval, publishing, monitoring, reporting, and issue resolution.

 - Establish the data foundation and measurement systems needed to understand marketplace adoption, conversion, solution quality, customer trust, and overall marketplace health.

 - Design scalable commercial models, policies, incentives, and partner economics with finance, legal, security, policy, and operations.

 - Establish standards and operating processes for solution quality, safety, compliance, performance, and lifecycle management.

 - Partner with ecosystem, sales, marketing, and customer success teams to ensure marketplace capabilities support partner participation and customer adoption.

 - Build and lead the marketplace team and operating cadence, aligning cross-functional owners around clear priorities, decisions, and outcomes.

Qualifications:

 - 10-15 years of experience in marketplaces, platforms, product, strategy, operations, ecosystems, or general management.

 - Proven experience building and scaling the product and operational foundation of a B2B marketplace or platform.

title: Member of Technical Staff - Post-Training (Reinforcement Learning & Generalization)
description:
WHO ARE WE?

Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company.  We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems.

We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.

We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft.

We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us!


Key Overview:
As a Member of Technical Staff in Post-Training, you will train our large language models (LLMs) with reinforcement learning and develop methods that help them generalize beyond the distribution they were trained on. You will design the training recipes, environments, and evaluations that tell us whether a model has truly learned a skill or has only fitted its training tasks, and turn what works into the recipes behind our production models. You will work closely with the post-training data infrastructure, evaluation, and pre-training teams.

Key Responsibilities

 - Design, run, and analyse large-scale RL post-training experiments (e.g., RLHF, RL from verifiable rewards).

 - Research and develop methods that improve out-of-distribution generalization, such as reward design, environment and task diversity, curricula, and regularization.

 - Build held-out evaluations that measure generalization to unseen tasks, domains, and formats, and that catch reward hacking and benchmark overfitting.

 - Diagnose training dynamics and failure modes, including instability, reward over-optimization, and capability regressions.

 - Turn successful research into robust, reproducible training recipes for production models.


Qualifications

 - Strong research and software engineering skills, with hands-on experience training LLMs.

 - Experience applying reinforcement learning to LLMs (e.g., PPO, GRPO, RLHF, RLVR), ideally at scale.

 - Track record of work on generalization, robustness, or distribution shift, through publications or shipped models.

 - Rigorous experimental practice: clean ablations, careful controls, and sound conclusions from noisy results.

 - Experience with distributed training (e.g., JAX, PyTorch, FSDP, Megatron) is a plus.

 - Excellent communication skills.

 - Deep understanding of data quality principles and best practices: demonstrates willingness to dive deep into data while possessing strong intuition for assessing the quality of datasets and anticipating how different data characteristics will impact model training outcomes.
   

Working Location
This role can be based remotely or from one of our office locations listed on the job description - there is no minimum in-office qualification requirement. We care most about hiring exceptional people regardless of locations, though please check the location listed on the posting for guidance around the core time zone or working hours alignment expected for the role.

title: Principal Engineer, Monetization Engineering
Senior Machine Learning Engineer, Voice Agents - EMEA Remote
description:
At Hugging Face, we're on a journey to democratize good AI. We are building the fastest growing platform for AI builders with over 11 million users who collectively shared over 3M+ models, 1M+ datasets & 1.47M+ apps. Our open-source libraries have more than 600k+ stars on Github.

About the Role

We are building the open voice-agent stack for Hugging Face, and we are looking for a senior engineer to own a large part of it.Two things sit at the centre of this role. The first is speech-to-speech, our open-source library for realtime voice agents. The second is hf-voice, a new product that will let any developer build and deploy voice agents with their Hugging Face account. 

The library already powers the Reachy Mini fleet and there is a public demo running on Spaces, so you won't start from a blank page. But almost everything about how this becomes a product developers rely on is still open, and you will have a direct say in it.

Your missions:

- Own the Open-Source Library:

  • Take architectural ownership of large parts of speech-to-speech: pipeline design, latency budget, and the reliability of the realtime loop.
  • Integrate new ASR, TTS and end-to-end speech models as they land, and keep the abstractions clean while the model landscape keeps moving.
  • Review community PRs, triage issues, cut releases, and grow the group of contributors around the project.

- Ship hf-voice:

  • Design the developer API and the streaming protocol: session lifecycle, transport (WebSockets/WebRTC), authentication, error semantics, versioning.
  • Build the serving side: realtime inference on GPU, concurrency, autoscaling, observability, and cost per session.
  • Work with the Hub and inference teams so that a working voice agent is easy to integrate into products and demos.
  • Take the product from demo to production: load testing, SLOs, graceful degradation when a model or a network path misbehaves.

- Work in the Open:

  • Write the docs, examples and templates that get a developer from zero to a running agent in minutes.
  • Support the deployments already relying on the stack, starting with the Reachy Mini fleet.
  • Talk about the work publicly if you enjoy it: blog posts, demos, conference talks. We cover the travel and the prep time.

Requirements

What we're looking for

  • Senior engineer, able to own a substantial part of an architecture and drive it forward autonomously.
  • Experience building developer-facing infrastructure at an AI or developer-tools company: inference APIs, agent infrastructure, or something comparable.
  • Substantial open-source contributions to a Python library. Comfortable with async Python and distributed systems, including their failure modes.
  • You have shipped something realtime: streaming, WebSockets or WebRTC, audio or video pipelines, live inference.
  • Practical experience with LLMs or multimodal models in production. Clear written communication and a habit of collaborating async and in public.
  • Motivated by voice and conversational AI.

Bonus points if you have

  • Contributions to a voice-agent framework such as speech-to-speech, pipecat, LiveKit Agents, Vocode or TEN.
  • Contributions to llama.cpp or another low-level inference runtime.
  • Hands-on work with ASR, TTS or end-to-end speech models, including evaluation of latency and quality trade-offs.
  • GPU serving, quantization, or on-device inference experience.
  • Audio pipeline knowledge: VAD, echo cancellation, jitter buffers, barge-in and turn detection.
  • Experience shipping to embedded or robotics targets.
  • A public track record: talks, blog posts, demos.

About You

If you're interested in joining us, but don't tick every box above, we still encourage you to apply! We're building a diverse team whose skills, experiences, and backgrounds complement one another. We're happy to consider where you might be able to make the biggest impact.

One more thing

At Hugging Face we believe great AI shouldn't require a massive cluster, we build for everyone, especially the GPU-poor. And because we read every application, here's a small sign that you read this one too: start your answer to the first application question with the words “GPU-poor and proud 🤗”. No trick, no catch, it just tells us a real person is on the other side.

Benefits

More about Hugging Face

We are actively working to build a culture that values diversity, equity, and inclusivity. We are intentionally building a workplace where people feel respected and supported—regardless of who you are or where you come from. We believe this is foundational to building a great company and community. Hugging Face is an equal opportunity employer and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.

We value development. You will work with some of the smartest people in our industry. We are an organization that has a bias for impact and is always challenging ourselves to continuously grow. We provide all employees with reimbursement for relevant conferences, training, and education.

We care about your well-being. We offer flexible working hours and remote options. We offer health, dental, and vision benefits for employees and their dependents. We also offer parental leave and flexible paid time off.

We support our employees wherever they are. While we have office spaces in NYC and Paris, we're very distributed and all remote employees have the opportunity to visit our offices. If needed, we'll also outfit your workstation to ensure you succeed.

We want our teammates to be shareholders. All employees have company equity as part of their compensation package. If we succeed in becoming a category-defining platform in machine learning and artificial intelligence, everyone enjoys the upside.

We support the community. We believe major scientific advancements are the result of collaboration across the field. Join a community supporting the ML/AI community.

title: Director of Detection and Response
description:
WHY HARVEY

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.

This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We’re scaling fast and defining a new category in real time. The work is ambitious, the bar is high, and the opportunity for growth — personal, professional, and financial — is unmatched.

Our team moves fast, takes ownership, and is deeply committed to the mission — operating with intensity, staying close to our customers, and pushing each other for excellence. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.




ROLE OVERVIEW

Harvey is building AI-native software for professional services. Our customers trust us with highly sensitive information and critical business workflows, making security fundamental to everything we build. We’re looking for a Director of Detection and Response to build and lead the team that identifies threats, responds decisively to incidents, and turns what we learn into stronger defenses.



You will own Harvey’s Detection and Response strategy, technical direction, and operational readiness across our production platform and corporate environment. Working with the CISO and leaders across Engineering, Infrastructure, IT, Legal, and Customer Trust, you’ll translate business risk into a focused program that protects customer data and enables Harvey to move quickly with confidence.



This is a technical leadership role for someone who can build an exceptional team, earn the trust of senior engineers, and bring clarity to high-stakes situations. You’ll develop a function that scales through software, automation, and strong partnerships, while staying close enough to the work to challenge detection designs and guide complex investigations.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Build and lead the organization. Hire and develop detection engineers, incident responders, and technical leaders; establish clear ownership and a culture of curiosity, sound judgment, and continuous learning. Own the roadmap, staffing plan, and investment decisions.

 - Own incident response and crisis readiness. Lead Harvey’s response to major security incidents, coordinating investigation, containment, recovery, and executive communication. Build clear severity criteria, escalation paths, playbooks, and sustainable 24/7 coverage for critical threats; develop incident commanders and cross-functional responders through exercises.

 - Build detection as an engineering capability. Set the technical direction for telemetry, detection pipelines, forensic tooling, and response automation across cloud, endpoint, identity, SaaS, and application environments. Apply software engineering practices to test detections, improve signal quality, and reduce manual work; evaluate AI-assisted investigation with measurable quality and appropriate human oversight.

 - Focus defenses on meaningful threats. Use threat intelligence, hunting, and an attacker’s perspective to prioritize scenarios that matter to Harvey, including account compromise, data theft, insider risk, privileged-access abuse, and abuse of AI-enabled workflows. Partner with offensive security and platform owners to validate coverage and close blind spots.

 - Make response a company capability. Partner with Engineering, IT, Legal, Privacy, Communications, and Customer Trust on sensitive investigations and crisis decisions. Establish clear escalation and decision authority, preserve evidence, and provide accurate findings to support Legal-led notification and disclosure decisions. Prepare cross-functional responders to contribute when incidents require broader support.

 - Turn incidents into lasting improvements. Drive blameless reviews and ensure corrective actions have owners, deadlines, and verified outcomes. Measure detection coverage, time to detect and contain, recurring failure modes, and responder workload, and use those results to guide investments and reduce customer impact.




WHAT YOU HAVE

 - Experience building and leading Detection and Response, incident response, or security engineering teams in a technology company with complex production systems. A record of hiring strong engineers, developing technical leaders, and scaling both the team and its operating model.

 - Deep incident response experience and demonstrated judgment during serious security events. You can lead investigations with incomplete information, make timely containment decisions, and communicate clearly with executives, engineers, and business partners. You bring composure, integrity, and discretion to sensitive investigations and decisions under scrutiny.

 - Strong technical foundations in cloud infrastructure, operating systems, networking, identity, and attacker tradecraft, with depth in detection engineering, threat hunting, or digital forensics. You understand how to investigate across corporate and production environments.

 - An engineering approach to security operations, backed by experience building detection platforms, investigation tools, or response automation. You can evaluate architecture and code, guide senior engineers, and make practical decisions about what to build, buy, or retire.

 - The ability to turn business risk into a focused strategy and deliver it through influence and partnership. You balance urgent response with long-term engineering work and build a demanding, supportive environment where people can do their best work.



Experience protecting enterprise SaaS, sensitive customer data, or AI/ML environments is especially valuable, as is experience investigating insider threats, partnering on privileged-access governance, or leading response under regulatory and public scrutiny.



At Harvey, you’ll shape how an AI company detects and responds to threats as its products and customers evolve. Your team’s work will directly protect customer trust and help make security a durable foundation for the business.




COMPENSATION

$280,000 - $385,000 USD

title: Senior Account Executive - Technology
description:
WHO ARE WE?

Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company.  We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems.

We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.

We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft.

We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us!


SENIOR ACCOUNT EXECUTIVE - TECHNOLOGY

Why this role? 

In this role, you will have ownership of the full sales cycle - from identifying leads to closing deals with Global 2000, large enterprises within the Technology sector. We're looking for an approachable and compelling communicator who loves working with prospects to uncover their needs and feels comfortable developing tailored value propositions around how Cohere's platform can help them achieve their business goals. You'll lay the foundation for Cohere's growth by owning your territory and collaborating with teammates across customer success, sales development, marketing, and solution architecture. You'll be the voice of the field and help our product and engineering teams prioritize the Cohere roadmap with customer-centric care. It's a highly self-directed role, so you should be someone who thrives in an unstructured and quickly evolving environment. And your opportunity for impact will be astronomical — Cohere has skies-the-limit potential, and you'll help us reach it.

As an Account Executive focused on the Technology sector you will:

 - Focus on net-new logo acquisition via outbound activity and relationship building with key stakeholders while also bringing a strong network of key decision-maker and influencer contacts and relationships in the vertical to accelerate engagements, drive strategic partnerships and win sales opportunities

 - Work closely with customers and prospects as a consultative, trusted advisor who deeply understands their challenges and goals, their technology ecosystem, and will tailor solutions to drive measurable impact for their businesses

 - Work in close partnership with channel partners to find opportunities to scale outreach and customer satisfaction in your region

 - Collaborate with product and engineering teams as well as customer success on strategic motions to deliver solutions to large enterprise customers

 - Collaborate with Sales Development Representatives to drive top of funnel activity

 - Own the full sales cycle – from initial outreach through proof-of-concept, deal close, and deployment; this is not a transactional sale that you can walk away from after the contract is signed but rather requires ongoing oversight of the project to ensure success

You may be a good fit if you have:

 - 8-12+ years of previous B2B sales experience with Global 2000, large enterprises in the Technology sector, negotiating and closing transformational multi-year (2-5 year) SaaS deals in the 7 figure range, and a track record of high performance and exceeding quota

 - Previous experience as a technical consultative salesperson, selling complex products, such as developer tools, API products, or AI / NLP solutions, are a plus, with a focus on applications in the Financial Services sector

 - Previous experience working with customers during the deployment phase of the engagement, aligning on how best to configure and customize the solution that supports success in production and builds trust to set up for expansion and growth

 - Previous experience working with channel partners such as cloud hyperscalers and system integrators to drive sales cycles and hit shared revenue goals

 - High tolerance for ambiguity - as an early sales hire, you'll have to be a self-starter, doer and a strategist who is capable of wearing many hats and doing what it takes to figure out a path to success

 - Curiosity - you want to go deep on NLP and become an expert on our technology while considering how to fit into a large organization's technology landscape with a focus on its applications in the Financial Services sectors

 - Fantastic communication skills - you are a great listener, have a knack for understanding what matters most to others, build strong relationships, can speak to the c-suite, and feel comfortable speaking to both technical and non-technical audiences in the Financial Services sector

Additional Requirements:

 - Deep understanding of the Technology industry, including key trends, challenges, and opportunities

 - Ability to articulate the value of AI and NLP solutions in the context of Financial Services operations.




FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES AT COHERE ENJOY THESE PERKS:

 - A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch.

 - Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health.

 - RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme.

 - 100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent.

 - Annual enrichment benefits:
   
   Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and a workspace improvement credit.
   
   Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching.

 - 6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days!)

 - Budget for traveling to other offices if you are remote, plus an annual company offsite.




HOW AND WHERE WE WORK:

title: Principal Software Engineer 2 - OLTP
description:
At Snowflake, we are powering the era of the agentic enterprise. To usher in this new era, we seek AI-native thinkers across every function who are energized by the opportunity to reinvent how they work. You don’t just use tools; you possess an innate curiosity, treating AI as a high-trust collaborator that is core to how you solve problems and accelerate your impact. We look for low-ego individuals who thrive in dynamic and fast-moving environments and move with an experimental mindset — who rapidly test emerging capabilities to discover simpler, more powerful ways to deliver results. At Snowflake, your role isn't just to execute a function, but to help redefine the future of how work gets done.


PRINCIPAL SOFTWARE ENGINEER 2 - OLTP

Snowflake is building the next generation of transactional systems for applications, AI and agents. Across Snowflake Postgres and Unistore, we are combining the performance, reliability and developer experience expected from modern operational databases with Snowflake's cloud-native architecture and governed data platform.

We're looking for a Principal Engineer 2 to help define and drive the architecture across database internals, storage, compute and cloud infrastructure. A core part of the role is designing transactional systems for agent-driven workloads, where isolated state, rapid database lifecycle, safe autonomous operations, and deep integration with enterprise data are first-class requirements.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Define and drive the long-term technical architecture for OLTP across Snowflake Postgres, Unistore and the infrastructure they depend on.

 - Lead major architectural decisions across transactions, storage, concurrency control, replication, recovery, query execution and database scalability.

 - Shape the compute and storage architecture for low-latency, highly available transactional systems, including resource isolation, elasticity, networking, caching and container infrastructure.

 - Build database primitives for agent-driven workloads, including fast creation of isolated transactional environments, checkpointing and rollback, and efficient lifecycle management.

 - Define how agents safely read and modify operational state, with strong guarantees around consistency, recovery, access control and governance.

 - Determine where PostgreSQL architecture and compatibility provide leverage and where alternative approaches can deliver meaningful advantages.

 - Design for workloads where databases and transactional environments are created and operated programmatically at machine speed rather than primarily through human administration.

 - Lead complex, cross-organizational engineering efforts and establish technical direction across multiple teams.

 - Work closely with product leaders, senior engineering leadership, and strategic customers on the most important technical and product decisions.

 - Raise the technical bar through architecture reviews, mentoring and hands-on leadership on the hardest systems problems.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - 15+ years of experience building databases, distributed systems, storage systems or large-scale cloud infrastructure, with sustained impact at significant technical scope.

 - Deep expertise in OLTP and database systems, including areas such as transactions, concurrency control, storage engines, indexing, query processing, replication, recovery and high availability.

 - Strong understanding of cloud infrastructure for low-latency stateful systems, including compute, storage, networking, resource isolation and failure handling.

 - Experience designing highly elastic, multi-tenant, or rapidly provisioned stateful systems where isolation and efficient lifecycle management are first-class concerns.

 - Strong instincts for how database architecture should evolve for AI-native applications and autonomous agents, including ephemeral state, sandboxing, safe transactional actions and programmatic database lifecycle.

 - Experience making difficult architectural tradeoffs across latency, throughput, consistency, availability, durability, scalability, isolation and cost.

 - A track record of taking technically ambitious systems from architecture through production at meaningful scale.

 - Experience influencing technical direction across multiple teams or a broad product area.
